title: Carcinoma Breast: current answers, not old keys
summary: Diagnose, stage and treat breast cancer the way today's papers ask, and unlearn the old PYQ keys.
closing: Triple assessment, stage by T and N, then match treatment to stage and receptors; when an old key disagrees, answer with today's practice.

objectives.text: Choose the current answers to 'most common' questions (cancer in women, site, type, subtype), rejecting the old cervix key
Tell invasive lobular from ductal carcinoma, and match BRCA1/BRCA2 to chromosome, tumour type and male breast cancer
Pick the triple-assessment components and the right imaging and tissue test for a breast lump, including why core biopsy beats FNAC
Decide who needs staging scans, and name the metastatic site and prognostic factor
Assign the T category from skin, chest-wall and inflammatory findings (peau d'orange, pectoralis, T4d)
Place nodal findings on the N ladder and say when disease is M1 (supraclavicular is N3c)
Choose between Halsted, MRM and breast conservation for an operable cancer, and tell Halsted from MRM
Decide BCS suitability, SLNB versus ALND, and radiotherapy after surgery
Pick the treatment sequence for locally advanced and inflammatory carcinoma
Choose the hormonal agent by menopausal status and predict tamoxifen and AI toxicity, chemoprevention and classic LCIS plan
Name the HER2 drug and its reversible cardiotoxicity, contrasted with doxorubicin
Predict the nerve deficit and complication after axillary dissection or mastectomy

traps.trap: FNAC is the investigation of choice for a breast lump
Supraclavicular node involvement is M1
Radical (Halsted) mastectomy is the standard surgery for operable carcinoma breast
Carcinoma cervix is the most common cancer in Indian women
A bone scan or CT is part of the routine work-up of every breast cancer
Trastuzumab cardiotoxicity is dose-dependent and irreversible like doxorubicin
Tamoxifen is the hormone of choice for every ER-positive patient
Invasive lobular carcinoma behaves like ductal (single mass, unilateral)
Peau d'orange means T4d (inflammatory carcinoma)
Invasion of pectoralis major alone is T4a chest-wall disease
Tumour larger than 5 cm is an absolute contraindication to BCS
Long thoracic nerve is the nerve most commonly injured in axillary dissection
Surgery first, then chemotherapy, in inflammatory or locally advanced cancer
Carcinoma is the most common cause of bloody nipple discharge
Clinically node-negative patients need ALND first, with SLNB only if it fails
BRCA1 is on 13q and BRCA2 on 17q
BRCA1 is the gene linked to male breast cancer
Mammography is the first imaging test for a woman under 35
Tamoxifen protects the endometrium
Classic LCIS needs mastectomy

segments.title: The old key versus now
segments.goal: Learner answers 'most common female cancer' and 'test for a lump' with old PYQ keys, fails, and sees what changed.

prefer.reason: Playbook: retrieval-gate hooks that let the learner fail a real stem first won 3/3.

segments.title: What it is and why it spreads
segments.goal: Build the model of histology, subtypes, BRCA genetics and lymphatic spread that later explains signs.

prefer.reason: Socratic ladder won the only mechanism trial; lets learner derive peau d'orange from lymphatic block.

segments.title: Reading the breast: clinical picture and work-up
segments.goal: Vignettes on lump, nipple, skin and node findings leading to triple assessment and the right test.

prefer.reason: Case-first vignette won clinical in the playbook; end on a multi-trap which-does-NOT-fit.

segments.title: Staging: T, N and M
segments.goal: Stage a case by laddering T and N, and decide whether scans are needed before calling M1.

prefer.reason: Faded worked example with skip lane wins diagnosis; put the why-probe before the fork.

segments.title: Surgery and the axilla
segments.goal: Choose operation, BCS suitability and axillary approach; link nerve injury to dissection.

prefer.reason: Erroneous example suits de-escalated surgery: spot the mistake in a Halsted or ALND-first plan.

segments.title: Systemic therapy and sequence
segments.goal: Pick the sequence for LABC and inflammatory disease, then the drug by receptor and menopausal status.

prefer.reason: Worked example then fade has won management 2/2.

segments.title: Exam traps: outdated keys and look-alikes
segments.goal: Face every high-yield trap again in a new form: old keys, T4 look-alikes, drug reversals, which-is-NOT.

prefer.reason: Exam-trap drill fits the four outdated-key traps and the which-is-NOT format.

segments.title: Put it together
segments.goal: Cold, mixed probes and a learner-built summary across diagnosis, staging, surgery and drugs.

prefer.reason: Retrieval gate with skip-if-correct lane won consolidate; playbook lesson from TOF S8.
